
# Lecture 3.1: Stieltjes Premeasures

## Characterization of Stieltjes Premeasures

Let $\mathcal{S}_{(]} = \{(a, b]: -\infty \le a \le b \le \infty\}$ be the canonical semi-algebra of left-open, right-closed intervals in $\mathbb{R}$, and let $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]}) = \mathcal{B}_{\text{el}}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the generated elementary field of finite disjoint unions of such intervals.

For a non-decreasing function $F: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$, the set function $\mu_F((a, b]) = F(b) - F(a)$ defines a well-defined finitely-additive measure $\mu_F$ on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]})$.

As established previously, if $F$ fails to be right-continuous at any point, $\mu_F$ fails to be countably additive. The converse also holds, yielding a full characterization.

::: {#thm-stieltjes-premeasure-characterization}
## Stieltjes Premeasure Theorem
The finitely-additive measure $\mu_F$ is a premeasure (i.e., countably additive) on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]})$ if and only if $F$ is right-continuous on $\mathbb{R}$:
$$
\lim_{\delta \downarrow 0} F(x + \delta) = F(x) \quad \text{for all } x \in \mathbb{R}.
$$ {#eq-right-continuity}
:::

To prove this theorem, we first establish a general criterion for countable additivity of a finitely-additive measure on a field generated by a semi-algebra.

## Countable Subadditivity Criterion on Semi-Algebras
Recall that a finitely-additive measure $\mu$ on a field $\mathcal{A}$ is countably superadditive; that is, for any countable collection of disjoint sets $\{A_n\}_{n=1}^\infty \subset \mathcal{A}$ with $A = \bigcup_{n=1}^\infty A_n \in \mathcal{A}$, we have:
$$
\mu(A) \ge \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mu(A_n).
$$
The following proposition shows that, for a finitely additive set function defined on the field generated by a semi-algebra, it is enough to verify countable subadditivity on the semi-algebra to obtain countable additivity on the entire field.


::: {#prp-countable-subadditivity-criterion}
## Countable Subadditivity Criterion
Let $\mathcal{S} \subseteq 2^\Omega$ be a semi-algebra over $\Omega$, and let $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$ be the generated field. A finitely-additive measure $\mu: \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}) \to [0, \infty]$ is a premeasure (countably additive) if and only if $\mu$ is countably subadditive on $\mathcal{S}$; that is, whenever $E = \bigcup_{n=1}^\infty E_n$ with $E, E_n \in \mathcal{S}$, we have:
$$
\mu(E) \le \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mu(E_n).
$$ {#eq-subadditivity-semialgebra}
:::

::: {.proof}
## Proof of @prp-countable-subadditivity-criterion
$(\Rightarrow)$ If $\mu$ is a premeasure on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$, it is countably additive on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$, which directly implies countable subadditivity on $\mathcal{S}$.

$(\Leftarrow)$ Finitely-additive measures are always countably superadditive on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$. Thus, to establish countable additivity, it suffices to prove that $\mu$ is countably subadditive on the entire field $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$.

Let $A = \bigcup_{n=1}^\infty A_n$ where $A, A_n \in \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$. By @prp-field-generated-by-semialgebra, any set in $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$ is a finite disjoint union of elements from $\mathcal{S}$. Thus, we can write:
$$
A = \bigcup_{j=1}^N E_j \quad \text{and} \quad A_n = \bigcup_{i=1}^{N_n} E_i^n,
$$
where $\{E_j\}_{j=1}^N \subset \mathcal{S}$ are pairwise disjoint, and for each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\{E_i^n\}_{i=1}^{N_n} \subset \mathcal{S}$ are pairwise disjoint.

For each fixed $j \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, since $E_j \subseteq A = \bigcup_{n=1}^\infty A_n$, we have:
$$
E_j = E_j \cap A = \bigcup_{n=1}^\infty (A_n \cap E_j) = \bigcup_{n=1}^\infty \bigcup_{i=1}^{N_n} (E_i^n \cap E_j).
$$

Since $\mathcal{S}$ is a semi-algebra, $E_i^n \cap E_j \in \mathcal{S}$. Applying countable subadditivity on $\mathcal{S}$ yields:
$$
\mu(E_j) \le \sum_{n=1}^\infty \sum_{i=1}^{N_n} \mu(E_i^n \cap E_j).
$$

Summing over $j = 1, \dots, N$ and using finite additivity on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$ gives:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu(A) = \sum_{j=1}^N \mu(E_j) &\le \sum_{j=1}^N \sum_{n=1}^\infty \sum_{i=1}^{N_n} \mu(E_i^n \cap E_j) \\
&= \sum_{n=1}^\infty \sum_{i=1}^{N_n} \sum_{j=1}^N \mu(E_i^n \cap E_j) \\
&= \sum_{n=1}^\infty \sum_{i=1}^{N_n} \mu\left( E_i^n \cap \bigcup_{j=1}^N E_j \right) \\
&= \sum_{n=1}^\infty \sum_{i=1}^{N_n} \mu(E_i^n \cap A) \\
&\le \sum_{n=1}^\infty \sum_{i=1}^{N_n} \mu(E_i^n) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mu(A_n).
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $\mu(A) \le \sum_{n=1}^\infty \mu(A_n)$, proving that $\mu$ is countably subadditive and hence a premeasure on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S})$. 
:::

## Proof of the Stieltjes Premeasure Theorem

We now prove @thm-stieltjes-premeasure-characterization by verifying countable subadditivity of $\mu_F$ on the semi-algebra $\mathcal{S}_{(]}$ using a Heine-Borel compactness argument.

::: {.proof}
## Proof of @thm-stieltjes-premeasure-characterization
Assume $F: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is right-continuous. By @prp-countable-subadditivity-criterion, it suffices to prove that $\mu_F$ is countably subadditive on $\mathcal{S}_{(]}$. 

Suppose $(a, b] \subseteq \bigcup_{j=1}^\infty (a_j, b_j]$ with $(a, b], (a_j, b_j] \in \mathcal{S}_{(]}$. If $a = b$ or $a > b$, $(a, b] = \emptyset$ and subadditivity holds trivially. Assume $-\infty < a < b < \infty$.

Fix $\epsilon > 0$ and $\delta > 0$ such that $a + \delta < b$. 

1. **Open Cover Construction:**
   The compact interval $[a + \delta, b]$ is contained in $(a, b]$:
   $$
   [a + \delta, b] \subset (a, b] \subseteq \bigcup_{j=1}^\infty (a_j, b_j].
   $$
   By right-continuity of $F$, for each $j \ge 1$, we can choose $\delta_j > 0$ such that:
   $$
   F(b_j + \delta_j) - F(b_j) < \frac{\epsilon}{2^j}.
   $$ {#eq-right-continuity-epsilon}
   Then $[a + \delta, b] \subset \bigcup_{j=1}^\infty (a_j, b_j + \delta_j)$.

2. **Compactness Argument:**
   Since $[a + \delta, b]$ is compact and $\{(a_j, b_j + \delta_j)\}_{j=1}^\infty$ is an open cover of $[a + \delta, b]$, there exists a finite subcover $N \in \mathbb{N}$ such that:
   $$
   [a + \delta, b] \subset \bigcup_{j=1}^N (a_j, b_j + \delta_j).
   $$
   This implies the interval cover $(a + \delta, b] \subseteq \bigcup_{j=1}^N (a_j, b_j + \delta_j]$.

3. **Finite Subadditivity and Limit Bounds:**
   By finite subadditivity of $\mu_F$ on interval unions, we have:
   $$
   \mu_F((a + \delta, b]) \le \sum_{j=1}^N \mu_F((a_j, b_j + \delta_j]).
   $$
   Using additivity $\mu_F((a_j, b_j + \delta_j]) = \mu_F((a_j, b_j]) + \mu_F((b_j, b_j + \delta_j])$, we obtain:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \mu_F((a + \delta, b]) &\le \sum_{j=1}^N \left( \mu_F((a_j, b_j]) + \mu_F((b_j, b_j + \delta_j]) \right) \\
   &\le \sum_{j=1}^\infty \mu_F((a_j, b_j]) + \sum_{j=1}^\infty \mu_F((b_j, b_j + \delta_j]).
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   Applying bound @eq-right-continuity-epsilon:
   $$
   \mu_F((a + \delta, b]) \le \sum_{j=1}^\infty \mu_F((a_j, b_j]) + \sum_{j=1}^\infty \frac{\epsilon}{2^j} = \sum_{j=1}^\infty \mu_F((a_j, b_j]) + \epsilon.
   $$

   Evaluating the left-hand side: $\mu_F((a + \delta, b]) = F(b) - F(a + \delta)$. Taking $\delta \downarrow 0$, right-continuity of $F$ at $a$ implies $F(a + \delta) \to F(a)$, yielding:
   $$
   \mu_F((a, b]) = F(b) - F(a) \le \sum_{j=1}^\infty \mu_F((a_j, b_j]) + \epsilon.
   $$
   Since $\epsilon > 0$ was arbitrary, letting $\epsilon \to 0$ gives:
   $$
   \mu_F((a, b]) \le \sum_{j=1}^\infty \mu_F((a_j, b_j]).
   $$

Extending to unbounded intervals ($a = -\infty$ or $b = \infty$) follows by taking limits. Thus $\mu_F$ is a premeasure on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]})$. $\blacksquare$
:::

## Lebesgue Premeasure and Translation Invariance

::: {#def-lebesgue-premeasure}
## Lebesgue Premeasure
When $F(x) = x$, the associated Stieltjes premeasure $\mu: \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]}) \to [0, \infty]$ is called the **Lebesgue premeasure**, satisfying:
$$
\mu((a, b]) = b - a.
$$ {#eq-lebesgue-interval}
:::

::: {#prp-translation-invariance}
## Translation Invariance of Lebesgue Premeasure
The Lebesgue premeasure $\mu$ is translation-invariant on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]})$. Specifically, for any $E \in \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]})$ and $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, if $E + \alpha := \{x + \alpha : x \in E\}$, then $E + \alpha \in \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]})$ and:
$$
\mu(E + \alpha) = \mu(E).
$$ {#eq-translation-invariance}
:::

::: {.proof}
## Proof of @prp-translation-invariance
Any set $E \in \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]})$ can be expressed as a finite disjoint union $E = \bigcup_{j=1}^n (a_j, b_j]$. Then $E + \alpha = \bigcup_{j=1}^n (a_j + \alpha, b_j + \alpha]$, which is also a finite disjoint union of elements in $\mathcal{S}_{(]}$.

By definition and finite additivity:
$$
\begin{align*}
\mu(E + \alpha) &= \sum_{j=1}^n \mu((a_j + \alpha, b_j + \alpha])\\
& = \sum_{j=1}^n ((b_j + \alpha) - (a_j + \alpha)) \\
&= \sum_{j=1}^n (b_j - a_j) = \sum_{j=1}^n \mu((a_j, b_j]) \\
&= \mu(E).
\end{align*}
$$

:::

---

## Takeaways
1. The Stieltjes premeasure $\mu_F$ is countably additive on the field $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]})$ if and only if $F$ is right-continuous.
2. The Lebesgue premeasure $\mu$ is translation-invariant on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]})$.
3. The Lebesgue premeasure $\mu$ is the unique translation-invariant premeasure on $\mathcal{A}(\mathcal{S}_{(]})$ satisfying $\mu((0, 1]) = 1$.
4. The Lebesgue premeasure $\mu$ can be extended to a complete measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R})$, known as the Lebesgue measure.
5. The Lebesgue measure is the unique translation-invariant measure on $\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{R})$ satisfying $\mu((0, 1]) = 1$.
